newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel - wet activity slow, paper leads way.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel - wet activity slow, paper leads way.

text.p: Physical fuel oil trading was limited on Friday with direction derived only from bouyant swaps.
Concern over the Middle East situation and the volatile crude market made dealers wary of getting tied into trades.
High sulphur barges edged higher with trades seen $1 up at $119 fob ARA, but eased down slightly in the afternoon. Those shippers forced to buy after holding back helped give support.
But, Russian straight run has been sold into the barge market which could knock out bullish talk of tightish supplies.
"The bubble could easily burst," said one trader.
High sulphur cargo activity was muted with most September needs seen covered. Prices were broadly steady around $108 fob NWE although a distressed cargo was rumoured done at $108 cif.
Low sulphur cargoes began to catch up with crude and paper prices showed a strong contango. Sept barrels were not heard offered and players turned to paper levels.
"If I had anything I wouldn't accept less than $120 fob NWE," said one trader.
A low sulphur barge was traded at $117.50 fob ARA in the morning.
